dispositions.title: Captured critical roll units
dispositions.conclusion: Machine Axis criticalRoll is an integer basis-point roll in [0,9999] and is always divided by 10000. Legacy normalized rolls use the explicit legacy-persisted-roll source path; value magnitude is never used as a format heuristic.
dispositions.remainingEvidenceBoundary: Captured client RNG stream identity remains external runtime evidence; the deterministic tool contract reproduces the verified distribution and threshold semantics.

dispositions.title: Raw public Schema boundary
dispositions.conclusion: Public CLI input is validated against the raw versioned JSON Schema before normalization, defaults, or coercion. Required fields, additional properties, and exact types produce structured issues; string false is rejected rather than coerced.
dispositions.remainingEvidenceBoundary: Trusted internal project objects continue through their existing adapter boundary and are not accepted as raw public CLI documents.

dispositions.title: Negative frame and horizon validation
dispositions.conclusion: Absolute and resolved relative schedules reject starts before frame zero, starts after the scenario horizon, and actions crossing the horizon. Frame zero remains valid and no downstream project draft clamps invalid input.

dispositions.title: Context-resolved action durations
dispositions.conclusion: Machine Axis uses a bounded two-stage stabilization loop: canonical compile and variant preflight resolve the actual form and effective occupancy before after-previous-end or after-action-end schedules are finalized. Ruby enhanced E1 resolves to 24 frames and state-derived Xiaoyu forms use their selected occupancy.
dispositions.remainingEvidenceBoundary: When the selected runtime form has no sourced effective duration, validation returns machine-axis-schedule-duration-unresolved instead of falling back to the public template.

dispositions.title: Shared scenario horizon
dispositions.conclusion: Actions and effect descriptors use the inclusive [0,duration] frame horizon. Events at T are retained, post-T commands and transitions are filtered before application, and terminal state describes time T only.

dispositions.title: Validation semantics
dispositions.conclusion: Validation separately reports schemaStatus, runnabilityStatus, and evidenceStatus. Scenario assumptions, unresolved execution conditions, source gaps, and unknown same-frame ordering are structured warnings and prevent evidence-closed classification.
dispositions.remainingEvidenceBoundary: A runnable-with-assumptions result is intentionally not evidence-closed and must retain its warning identities.

dispositions.title: Evaluation conservation
dispositions.conclusion: Totals, byAction, and byActor use the same combat-hit filter. The evaluation separates combatHitCount, stateEventCount, inflictedToughnessDamage, recoveredToughness, and netToughnessDamage; recovery ticks are not action hits or negative inflicted damage.

dispositions.title: Duplicate Kibo runtime ownership
dispositions.conclusion: Product contract confirms that different actors may equip the same Kibo species. Cooldown and resource ownership are isolated by runtime entity actorId plus kiboId, so two same-species Kibo actions execute independently instead of sharing species cooldown state.

dispositions.title: Deterministic same-frame ordering
dispositions.conclusion: Runtime descriptors compare integer absoluteFrame, explicit phase priority, runtime priority, and source sequence. timeMs and action identity are no longer ordering tiebreakers. Unknown simultaneous actor/Kibo input ordering is exposed as a scenario warning.
dispositions.remainingEvidenceBoundary: A cross-owner same-frame input without verified phase or explicit scenario order remains evidence-open; the engine does not invent an action-ID winner.
